story_title: The Deadliest Natural Disasters: A Century of Loss and Trends
story_subtitle: Analyzing the impact of natural disasters on global mortality from 1900 to 2017

story_pieces.narration: Total deaths from natural disasters fluctuated dramatically over the 20th century, peaking in 1931 with 3.7 million deaths from droughts. The 1900s saw the highest mortality, followed by a gradual decline in the latter half of the century.
story_pieces.question: How has the total number of deaths from natural disasters changed over the 20th and 21st centuries?
story_pieces.visualization: line chart (year vs. total deaths for 'All natural disasters')

story_pieces.narration: Droughts caused the most cumulative deaths (over 25 million) across all years, surpassing earthquakes, extreme weather, and other disaster types. Epidemics also contributed significantly, with over 10 million deaths recorded.
story_pieces.question: Which disaster type has caused the most deaths overall?
story_pieces.visualization: bar chart (disaster type vs. total deaths)

story_pieces.narration: The deadliest year in recorded history was 1931, with 3.7 million deaths attributed to droughts. Other notable years include 1917 (2.5 million deaths from epidemics) and 1920 (over 2.5 million deaths from droughts and epidemics combined).
story_pieces.question: Which year had the highest number of deaths from natural disasters?
story_pieces.visualization: bar chart (year vs. deaths for top disaster types)

story_pieces.narration: The 1930s accounted for over 10 million deaths, driven by extreme droughts, earthquakes, and epidemics. By contrast, the 2000s saw fewer than 2 million total deaths, reflecting a possible decline in large-scale disaster mortality.
story_pieces.question: How have the contributions of different disaster types to total deaths changed over decades?
story_pieces.visualization: stacked bar chart (decade vs. deaths by disaster type)

story_pieces.narration: Recent decades (2000s-2010s) show a decreasing trend in natural disaster-related deaths, despite increased population and urbanization. This may be due to better early warning systems, disaster preparedness, or improved response mechanisms.
story_pieces.question: Has there been a decline in deaths from natural disasters in recent years, and if so, what factors might contribute to this trend?
story_pieces.visualization: line chart (year vs. total deaths for 'All natural disasters') with trendline
